title: Research: the W3C traceparent format and the OpenTelemetry Python SDK's trace-context propagator are kb facts
goal: kb/public/logs/otel-python-sdk.md gains facts with source rows on the W3C Trace Context traceparent header (version 00, a 32-hex trace-id, a 16-hex parent-id, the trace-flags byte with the sampled bit, the all-zero ids that are invalid, and tracestate) from the W3C Recommendation (DOC), and on how the Python SDK's TraceContextTextMapPropagator reads and writes it from a carrier such as an environment dict (CODE at a pinned commit), so a tool can hand a child process the context of a span it built with explicit ids

run:
import subprocess, sys
ART = 'kb/public/logs/otel-python-sdk.md'
CASES = [('What is the format of the W3C traceparent header: version, trace-id, parent-id and trace-flags?', ['traceparent', 'trace-id', 'parent-id']), ('Which trace-flags bit marks a W3C traceparent as sampled?', ['sampled', 'trace-flags'])]
miss = []
for q, terms in CASES:
    out = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '_tools/rag.py', 'pack', q, '--root', 'public', '--budget', '2500'],
                         capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    hit = [l for l in out.splitlines() if l.startswith('- ' + ART[len('kb/'):] + ':') and '[DOC' in l
           and all(t.lower() in l.lower() for t in terms)]
    if not hit:
        miss.append((q, terms))
print('missing:', miss if miss else 'none')
sys.exit(1 if miss else 0)
